summary:
The Investing in All of America Act of 2025 (Pub. L. 119-92, enacted May 19, 2026, from H.R. 2066) amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to modify the definitions and maximum-leverage provisions governing Small Business Investment Companies (SBICs), principally to exclude from statutory leverage limits certain investments in enterprises located in rural or low-income areas, small businesses in critical technology areas, and small manufacturers.

Section 2(a) amends the definition of "private capital" in Section 103(9) (15 U.S.C. 662(9)). It strikes the requirement in subparagraph (B)(iii)(I) that a state or local government entity be "established prior to October 1, 1987," and expands subclause (II) to include a "foundation, endowment, or trust of any college or university" alongside pension plans. It adds a new subparagraph (C) providing that private capital does not include funds obtained directly or indirectly from any Federal, State, or local government or governmental agency or instrumentality—except funds described in subclauses (I)–(III) of subparagraph (B)(iii)—for purposes of the Administrator's approval of leverage requests.

Section 2(b) amends the maximum-leverage provisions of Section 303(b)(2) (15 U.S.C. 683(b)(2)). For a single licensee (subparagraph (A)), it reduces the private-capital multiplier in clause (i) from 300 percent to 200 percent, and revises the dollar cap in clause (ii) to $250,000,000 for a company making quarterly or semiannual interest payments, or $175,000,000 for any other company licensed under section 301(c). For commonly controlled companies (subparagraph (B)), it replaces the single $350,000,000 cap with a tiered structure: $475,000,000 for commonly controlled companies making quarterly or semiannual interest payments, or $350,000,000 for other commonly controlled companies licensed under section 301(c).

Section 2(b)(3) revises subparagraph (C)'s leverage-exclusion provision. The heading is broadened to cover rural areas, critical technology areas, and small manufacturers. Clause (i) is restructured (subject to clause (iii)) to exclude from outstanding-leverage calculations (for purposes of subparagraphs (A) and (B)) amounts invested in: (I) small business concerns in low-income geographic areas (as defined in section 351) or rural areas (as defined in 7 U.S.C. 1991(a)(13)); (II) small business concerns operating primarily in a covered technology category (as defined in 10 U.S.C. 149(e)); or (III) small manufacturers (as defined in section 501(e)(6)). Amended clause (ii) caps the aggregate exclusion at the lesser of 50 percent of private capital or $125,000,000, while preserving the subparagraph (A)(i) limitation and consistency with a section 301(c) leverage-determination ratio. Amended clause (iii) establishes prospective applicability: an investment qualifies for exclusion only if made after the clause's date of enactment.

The Act contains no appropriation.
